name: Katanga

flag.description: Divided diagonally by a green band running from the lower hoist to the upper fly, with red above and white below, and three red crosses in the white lower fly.
flag.symbolism: The three red crosses are Katanga crosses, the cross-shaped copper ingots once used as currency in the region, a reference to its copper wealth.

hook: Katanga split its flag diagonally with a green band, red above and white below, and put three red copper-ingot crosses in the white corner.
trivia: Katanga, led by Moïse Tshombe, declared independence from the newly independent Congo on 11 July 1960; no country recognised it, and UN forces ended the secession in January 1963.
UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld was killed in a plane crash in 1961 while travelling to negotiate a ceasefire in the Katanga conflict.
